mainEntity.name: Are Local Services Ads worth it for a small local business?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can be, if you qualify, you answer your phone, and you close the leads you get. The model protects you from paying for clicks that never call. It does not protect you from leads that do not turn into jobs. Measure booked jobs and cost per booked job, not lead count.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay for bad leads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google assesses each lead when the customer first reaches out and does not charge for leads it finds invalid or low quality. If you believe a charged lead was low quality, use the Feedback Survey for that lead. Google may also issue credits automatically when its models later judge a lead to be low quality.

mainEntity.name: What happened to the Google Guaranteed badge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google's current Local Services help pages call the trust badge the Google Verified badge, and describe it as the sign that a business passed Google's screening. If you see Google Guaranteed on older articles, check the advice against Google's current help pages.

mainEntity.name: How do I set a budget for Local Services Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: You set an average weekly budget based on the number of leads you want in a typical week. After an account moves into Google Ads, Google divides that historical weekly budget by 7 to set a daily average budget. Start from the number of jobs you can actually take on.

mainEntity.name: Can I run Local Services Ads and Google Search Ads at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many local service businesses use both, because they capture different searches. Track each one separately so you can see which produces booked jobs at a cost you can afford.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a website for these ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Search Ads send people to a landing page, so yes. For Local Services Ads, your Google Business Profile and your reviews do a lot of the trust work, but a clear website still helps people who look you up before they call. Build the foundation first, then add spend.
